text:
Good afternoon. It is Tuesday, October twentieth, twelve thirty in the afternoon. 

First, the news from home.

Story one. Joy Online reports that the opposition National Democratic Congress has reversed its directive that asked Zakaria Abdulai, the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School, to withdraw from the party's constituency chairmanship race over sexual abuse allegations. The party's Deputy General Secretary, Mustapha Gbande, explained that this decision was taken to protect the aspirant's rights while investigations continue, but he stressed that the N D C will not hesitate to sanction or remove Abdulai even before the probe ends or after he wins.

Story two. According to Graphic Online, the flagbearer of the New Patriotic Party, Doctor Mahamudu Bawumia, has challenged the government to translate reported economic gains into tangible relief for ordinary households. Speaking at the party's National Thanksgiving Service, Doctor Bawumia argued that true economic success must be measured by the ability of citizens to afford basic needs like rent, fuel, electricity, water, and transport, rather than relying solely on official statistics.

Story three. Graphic Online also reports that the Coalition of Domestic Election Observers has urged the government to reform the appointment process for the leadership of the Electoral Commission. The election observer group pointed to recommendations from the Constitution Review Committee for an open and merit-based selection involving a reformed Council of State, the Public Services Commission, and parliamentary approval, expressing concern that the government previously rejected these proposals.

Now, around the world.

Story four. Major international outlets, including France twenty-four, the Guardian, and Deutsche Welle, report that voters in the Canadian province of Alberta have decisively rejected a proposal to hold a referendum on declaring independence from Canada. The vote delivers a major victory for unity under Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, with official counts showing roughly seventy-six percent voting to remain within the country.

Story five. According to the Guardian and France twenty-four, an Australian federal lawmaker, Helen Haines, has been critically injured in what authorities describe as a deliberate attack by a man driving a vehicle. A suspect has been arrested and charged with intentionally causing serious injury, drawing wide political condemnation across Australia as the lawmaker remains hospitalised following emergency surgery.

You can open Dad News and ask for more about any story by its number.
